title: Writing messages, and saying goodbye
goal: Writing short messages and simple letters, recognizing the two big dialects of Pashto — and closing twenty units with a way of saying goodbye that doesn't sound like a translation.
bekal: write short messages and simple letters in Pashto
recognize the Kandahar and Kabul dialects and pick one
say goodbye, give thanks, and promise to come back

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — د تګ ورځ
dialogs.intro: The last morning. The bags are by the door, the car is waiting in the lane, and three months suddenly feel like three days.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نو نن ځې. وخت ډېر ژر تېر شو.
lines.baca: no nən dze. wakht ḍer zhər ter shū.
lines.id: So you're leaving today. Time went by so fast.
lines.literal: so today go-you. time very quickly past became.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: هو. درې میاشتې وې، خو درې ورځې ښکاري.
lines.baca: ho. dre myāshte we, kho dre wradze ṣkārī.
lines.id: Yes. Three months, but it feels like three days.
lines.literal: yes. three months were, but three days seems.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: حتماً. انشاءالله بل پسرلی به راشم، د نوروز لپاره.
lines.baca: hatman. inshā'allāh bəl psarlay ba rāshəm, də Nawroz ləpāra.
lines.id: Definitely. God willing, I'll come next spring, for Nowruz.
lines.literal: definitely. God-willing other spring will come-I, of Nowruz for.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نو مونږ به مزار ته لاړ شو. هلته نوروز تر ټولو لوی وي.
lines.baca: no mūẓ ba Mazār ta lāṛ shū. halta Nawroz tər ṭolo loy wī.
lines.id: Then we'll go to Mazar. Nowruz there is the biggest.
lines.literal: so we will Mazar to going become-we. there Nowruz from all big usually-is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه به تاسو ته لیک ولیکم. په پښتو!
lines.baca: zə ba tāso ta līk wə́likəm. pə paṣto!
lines.id: I'll write you a letter. In Pashto!
lines.literal: I will you to letter write-I. in Pashto!

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: غلطۍ به ولري، خو مونږ به پوه شو.
lines.baca: ghalatəy ba wə́larī, kho mūẓ ba poh shū.
lines.id: It'll have mistakes, but we'll understand.
lines.literal: mistakes will have-it, but we will understanding become-we.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: یوه پوښتنه لرم. ولې کندهار کې ښه وایي او دلته خه؟
lines.baca: yawa pūṣtəna larəm. wale Kandahār ke ṣa wāyī aw dəlta kha?
lines.id: I have a question. Why do they say ṣa in Kandahar and kha here?
lines.literal: one question have-I. why Kandahar in ṣa say-they and here kha?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: دوه لهجې دي. جنوب او ختیځ. دواړه سمې دي.
lines.baca: dwa lahje dī. janūb aw khatīdz. dwāṛa same dī.
lines.id: There are two dialects. Southern and eastern. Both are correct.
lines.literal: two dialects are. south and east. both correct are.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: هغه چې ډېره اورې. خو یوه غوره کړه او مه یې بدلوه.
lines.baca: hagha che ḍera awre. kho yawa ghwara kṛa aw ma ye badalawa.
lines.id: The one you hear most. But pick one and don't switch.
lines.literal: that which much hear-you. but one choice do and don't it change.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ستاسو مېلمستیا زه هېڅکله نه هېروم. مننه، د هر څه لپاره.
lines.baca: stāso melmastyā zə hetskəla nə herawəm. manana, də har tsə ləpāra.
lines.id: I'll never forget your hospitality. Thank you, for everything.
lines.literal: of-yours hospitality I never not forget-I. thank-you, of every thing for.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: دا کور ستا دی. هر وخت راشه.
lines.baca: dā kor stā day. har wakht rāsha.
lines.id: This house is your house. Come any time.
lines.literal: this house yours is. every time come.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: خدای پامان. په مخه مو ښه.
lines.baca: khudāy pāmān. pə makha mo ṣa.
lines.literal: God protection. with front yours good.

notes: The sentence دا کور ستا دی — "this house is your house" — is not mere politeness. Under مېلمستیا, someone who has once been a guest keeps a place, and the offer has no expiry date. The right answer isn't to refuse it but to accept it with مننه.

⚠️ The dialect difference Budi asks about is what confuses beginners most. The letter **ښ** is read *ṣ* in the south (Kandahar, Helmand, Quetta) and like **kh** in the east and north (Kabul, Jalalabad, Peshawar). Likewise **ږ** is read *ẓ* in the south and like **g** in the east.

Zarghuna's advice is the best advice in this module: pick one dialect and stick with it. What sounds odd to native speakers isn't your choice but switching back and forth mid-sentence. If you're headed for Kabul, use the Kabul pronunciation; if Kandahar, use Kandahar's.

The word غلطي means "mistake", and غلطۍ به ولري is a very common admission. Afghans almost never correct a foreigner's grammar unless asked — they consider it impolite. If you want to be corrected, ask: **زما غلطۍ راته ووایه**.

The form وې in درې میاشتې **وې** is past "to be" for a feminine plural subject. The word میاشت (month) is feminine, its plural is میاشتې, so the verb is وې. Note that this form differs from وو, used for masculine plurals.
The farewell په مخه مو ښه literally means "may the road ahead of you be good", and it's said to someone leaving. The reply is مننه, or more warmly: **خدای دې مل شه** — "may God be your companion".

grammars.title: Writing short messages and letters
body: A Pashto letter opens with a greeting and a blessing, not straight with the content. That opening isn't a formality you can skip; leaving it out makes your letter feel like a notice, not a letter.
Text messages are much looser and often use spoken forms. What stays even in the shortest message is a greeting at the start and a blessing at the end.

grammars.title: Two dialects, and how to pick one
body: The biggest differences lie in four letters, and you can hear all of them in a single sentence. Other differences are in vocabulary and endings, but these four letters instantly show where you learned.
The standard written language is the same for both. Only the sound differs, so whichever you choose, you read Pashto writing with exactly the same letters.

sections.title: Messages, greetings, and what you take home

blocks.text: A sample short message you can copy
The message below uses only vocabulary from the twenty units of this module. There isn't a single word in it you haven't seen, and that's proof you can already write in Pashto.

head: Message to the host, after getting home
Meaning
rows: زه روغ رسېدم. سفر اوږد و، خو ښه و.
I arrived safely. The trip was long, but good.
ستاسو مېلمستیا مې هېڅکله نه هېروم.
کور ته مې سلامونه ورسوه — مور، پلار او ګلالۍ ته.
Give my regards to everyone at home — to your mother, father, and Gulalai.
God willing, I'll come next spring.

blocks.title: What you have after twenty units
items: You can **introduce yourself** and ask how people are at the right level of politeness, without ever tripping between ته and تاسو.
You can **haggle at the bazaar** with numbers where the units come first, and know when to haggle and when not to.
You can **make plans** for tomorrow with به, and **tell about yesterday** — including the ما rule that flips the whole past sentence.
You can **explain where it hurts** to a doctor, **ask the way** from a stranger, and **turn down a second helping** without offending anyone.
And most important: you can **read the script**, including the eight letters that neither Arabic nor Persian has. That's a door that will never close again.

blocks.title: Three things no page can teach
items: **Your patience is worth more than your vocabulary.** Afghans will wait for your sentence to finish, however hard it comes out, and won't finish it for you.
**Speaking Pashto opens doors English doesn't.** In big cities many people speak English; few foreigners make the effort with Pashto, and that effort is what people remember.

**You'll be treated as a guest.** That's not a reward for your fluency but part of a code of life older than any country. There's only one thing you can give back: try your hardest, and say **مننه** and mean it.
Give my regards to everyone at home.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the missing parts of the letter.
Say how these words are pronounced in Kandahar and in Kabul.
Put the words in the right order.
